newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, France to bid to make Airbus planes.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, France to bid to make Airbus planes.

text.p: Taiwan's state-run Aerospace Industrial Development and France's Latecore will bid jointly to make planned new planes for European consortium Airbus Industrie, officials said on Thursday.

"Aerospace Industrial Development has reached agreement with Latecore to jointly bid for the right to design and manufacture Airbus' planned AIR-84, AIR-70 and AIR-58 planes," said Jack Tang, deputy director of the economics ministry's Committee for Aviation and Space Industy development.
"Several groups will join the bids and Airbus is expected to announce bidding results in June or July," Tang told Reuters.
Details of the joint bid were confidential, he said.

Aerospace Industrial Development, owned by the economics ministry, said on Thurday it would sign an agreement on Saturday with Aero Vodochody of the Czech Republic to jointly manufacture small passenger airplanes.
Aerospace Industrial Development, long a non-commercial military plane manufacturing centre, was converted into a state-run company in July 1996.
